title: CVE-2023-38545: socks5 heap buffer overflow
excerpt:
# Summary:

The SOCKS5 state machine can be manipulated by a remote attacker to overflow heap memory if four conditions are met:

1. The request is made via socks5h.
2. The state machine's negotiation buffer is smaller than ~65k.
3. The SOCKS server's "hello" reply is delayed.
4. The attacker sets a final destination hostname larger than the negotiation
buffer.

libcurl is supposed to disable SOCKS5 remote hostname resolution for hostnames larger than 255 but will not due to a state machine bug.

For example tor user running libcurl app with follow location that connects to rogue onion server that replies with payload in `Location:` header which causes crash or worse.

# Walkthrough:

`do_SOCKS` initializes local variable `socks5_resolve_local` depending on the `CURLPROXY_` name. There are two relevant names for this state machine:

- `CURLPROXY_SOCKS5` (SOCKS5 with local resolve of dest host)
- `CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME` (SOCKS5 with remote resolve of dest host)

[Code:](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-8_3_0/lib/socks.c#L573-L574)
~~~c
  bool socks5_resolve_local =
    (conn->socks_proxy.proxytype == CURLPROXY_SOCKS5) ? TRUE : FALSE;
~~~

For this scenario, `CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME` is the name and `socks5_resolve_local` is initialized FALSE.

The `do_SOCKS` state machine is entered for the first time for the connection. `sx->state` is `CONNECT_SOCKS_INIT` (which happens to be the first label). In that state the hostname length is checked and if too long to resolve remotely (>255) then it sets `socks5_resolve_local` to TRUE.

[Code:](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-8_3_0/lib/socks.c#L588-L593)
~~~c
    /* RFC1928 chapter 5 specifies max 255 chars for domain name in packet */
    if(!socks5_resolve_local && hostname_len > 255) {
      infof(data, "SOCKS5: server resolving disabled for hostnames of "
            "length > 255 [actual len=%zu]", hostname_len);
      socks5_resolve_local = TRUE;
    }
~~~

The local variable `socks5_resolve_local` is changed but, because this is a state machine, subsequent calls to `do_SOCKS` are in a different state and do not make the same change. ==**This is the bug.**==

For this scenario, the hostname is longer than 255 characters and `do_SOCKS` is on a subsequent call, which means `socks5_resolve_local` remains FALSE. This can happen by chance or be forced by an attacker.

summary: The SOCKS5 state machine can be manipulated to overflow heap memory when using socks5h with a hostname longer than 255 characters, due to a bug where remote resolution is not disabled on subsequent state machine calls.

claims.text: The SOCKS5 state machine fails to disable remote hostname resolution for hostnames longer than 255 characters on subsequent calls, leading to a heap buffer overflow.
claims.reasoning: The local variable socks5_resolve_local is re-initialized to FALSE on every call to do_SOCKS5 for CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME. The hostname length check (>255) only runs in CONNECT_SOCKS_INIT state (first call). On subsequent calls when the state machine is in CONNECT_SOCKS_READ waiting for server reply, the check is skipped. When the server finally replies, the state transitions to CONNECT_REQ_INIT which reads the re-initialized FALSE value, then goes to CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE where the hostname is copied into socksreq (data->state.buffer) without bounds checking.

citations.note: socks5_resolve_local initialized as local variable based on proxy type
CONNECT_SOCKS_INIT state where hostname length check runs
Length check only executes in CONNECT_SOCKS_INIT state
CONNECT_REQ_INIT reads socks5_resolve_local which was re-initialized to FALSE
CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE copies hostname without length validation

claims.text: The flaw occurs in the CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE state where the hostname is copied into the socksreq buffer without length validation.
claims.reasoning: In CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE (lines 904-911), the code assumes hostname_len <= 255 (per RFC1928) and copies it into socksreq which aliases data->state.buffer. No bounds check against the buffer size is performed.

citations.note: CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE state copies hostname via memcpy
hostname_len used as one-byte length and memcpy size

claims.text: An attacker controlling a SOCKS server can delay the initial hello reply and force a hostname longer than 255 characters to trigger the overflow.
claims.reasoning: An attacker controlling a SOCKS server can delay the initial hello reply (keeping state in CONNECT_SOCKS_READ). Combined with a redirect (CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION) providing a hostname >255 chars (up to 65535), when the server finally replies the state machine proceeds with socks5_resolve_local=FALSE into CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE.

citations.note: CONNECT_SOCKS_READ state waits for server reply via socks_state_recv
On valid reply (method 0), transitions to CONNECT_REQ_INIT
Hostname can be up to MAX_URL_LEN (65535) characters

claims.text: Heap buffer overflow can corrupt adjacent memory, potentially leading to remote code execution or application crash.
claims.reasoning: Default buffer is 16385 bytes. Hostname can be 65535 bytes. The memcpy in CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE writes hostname_len bytes plus 2 bytes (type + length) into the buffer without checking remaining space, causing heap overflow when hostname exceeds buffer capacity.

claims.text: By using curl with CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION and a malicious Location header containing a long hostname, while delaying the SOCKS server hello, the overflow can be reproduced.
claims.reasoning: The reproduction steps are plausible: CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION allows attacker-controlled redirect with long hostname in Location header; socks5h proxy uses CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME; delaying SOCKS server hello keeps state machine in CONNECT_SOCKS_READ until the redirect is processed.

claims.text: The exploit requires knowledge of the buffer size (e.g., 16384+1) and can be triggered with a hostname exceeding the remaining buffer space.
claims.reasoning: The exploit requires hostname length exceeding the remaining buffer space. With default 16384+1 buffer, a hostname >~16KB triggers overflow. The report correctly identifies buffer size configurations.

key_reasons: Local variable socks5_resolve_local re-initialized on each do_SOCKS5 call, losing the >255 hostname check result from CONNECT_SOCKS_INIT
State machine can be delayed in CONNECT_SOCKS_READ by malicious SOCKS server
CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE copies hostname into data->state.buffer without bounds check
Default buffer (16385 bytes) smaller than max hostname (65535 bytes), enabling heap overflow
Attacker can trigger via redirect (CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION) with long hostname while SOCKS server delays hello reply
reply: The report correctly identifies a heap buffer overflow in the SOCKS5 state machine. The bug is that socks5_resolve_local is a local variable re-initialized on each do_SOCKS5 call, so the >255 hostname check in CONNECT_SOCKS_INIT (line 588-593) is lost when the state machine later reaches CONNECT_RESOLVE_REMOTE (line 904-911). An attacker controlling a SOCKS server and a redirect can delay the hello reply and supply a hostname exceeding the default 16KB buffer, causing memcpy to overflow data->state.buffer. This is a valid security vulnerability.
